newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ-USDA Florida orange data seen mainly neutral.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ-USDA Florida orange data seen mainly neutral.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Florida citrus crop estimate was in line with industry expectations, market sources said, and should have little effect on frozen concentrated orange juice futures.
The USDA's first estimate for the 1996/97 Florida crop came in at record high of 220 million 90-lb boxes, up from last year's total of 203.2 million boxes.
Florida crop yield rose to 1.53 gallons per box from 1.52 per box last season, the USDA reported.
Industry analysts had expected the USDA to raise output between 215 million and 225 million boxes.

"It is neutral. There are no surprises," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. Ganes had expected the crop to come in between 220 and 225 million boxes due to a larger and more mature tree population in Florida.
But Fimat Futures analyst Kevin Marshburn said the rise in crop yield, as well as, an increase in output from an early forecast by consultant Elizabeth Steger, could prove slightly bearish.
Steger's estimate in August put the 1996/97 Florida crop at 215.0 million boxes.
"It is neutral to negative," said Marshburn. "It is five million boxes more than the private estimate of Elizabeth Steger. Also, it's a pretty good yield."
Another analyst called the report neutral to slightly bearish, and said that while the crop figures were largely filtered into the futures market, they could limit the upside of the market.
But the analyst also noted that Thursday's FCOJ weekly movement may have more of an impact an the futures market.

The Florida Citrus Processors Association said frozen concentrated orange juice movement into trade channels for the week ended October 5 was 4,004,866 gallons compared with 5,100,274 gallons last week.
"The poor movement yesterday does not bode well for the market," the analyst said. "It creates concern on the demand side."
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1640
